content:
Below is an idiomatic way to add this in a Flux + kustomize repo, assuming the repo’s existing AWS resources actually use the `*.aws.upbound.io` CRDs as your note says.

If your repo truly uses ACK API groups like `s3.services.k8s.aws`, say so and I’ll convert this 1:1. The structure stays the same.

---

## What to add

### New directories
- `infra/s3/logs/`
- `infra/iam/logs-irsa/`

### Updated overlays
- `overlays/dev/`
- `overlays/prod/`

### Updated Flux
- add a dedicated Flux `Kustomization` for the logs bucket

---

# 1) S3 logs bucket base

## `infra/s3/logs/kustomization.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - bucket.yaml
  - versioning.yaml
  - encryption.yaml
  - public-access-block.yaml
```

## `infra/s3/logs/bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: logs
spec:
  forProvider:
    region: us-east-1
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default
```

## `infra/s3/logs/versioning.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: BucketVersioning
metadata:
  name: logs
spec:
  forProvider:
    bucketSelector:
      matchLabels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: logs-bucket
    region: us-east-1
    versioningConfiguration:
      - status: Enabled
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default
```

## `infra/s3/logs/encryption.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: BucketServerSideEncryptionConfiguration
metadata:
  name: logs
spec:
  forProvider:
    bucketSelector:
      matchLabels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: logs-bucket
    region: us-east-1
    rule:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          - sseAlgorithm: AES256
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default
```

## `infra/s3/logs/public-access-block.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: BucketPublicAccessBlock
metadata:
  name: logs
spec:
  forProvider:
    bucketSelector:
      matchLabels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: logs-bucket
    region: us-east-1
    blockPublicAcls: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicAcls: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default
```

### Important
Add labels to the bucket so the selector works.

Update `infra/s3/logs/bucket.yaml` to:

```yaml
apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: logs
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: logs-bucket
spec:
  forProvider:
    region: us-east-1
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default
```

---

# 2) IRSA IAM role base

This creates:
- an IAM policy granting read/write to the logs bucket
- an IAM role with web identity trust for IRSA
- a Kubernetes service account annotated with the role ARN

Because OIDC issuer, account ID, bucket name, and namespace are env-specific, keep the base generic and patch in overlays.

## `infra/iam/logs-irsa/kustomization.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - policy.yaml
  - role.yaml
  - role-policy-attachment.yaml
  - serviceaccount.yaml
```

## `infra/iam/logs-irsa/policy.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: logs-irsa-policy
spec:
  forProvider:
    name: logs-irsa-policy
    description: Read/write access to logs bucket
    policy: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Sid": "ListBucket",
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": [
              "s3:ListBucket"
            ],
            "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::REPLACE_BUCKET_NAME"
          },
          {
            "Sid": "ObjectRW",
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": [
              "s3:GetObject",
              "s3:PutObject",
              "s3:DeleteObject"
            ],
            "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::REPLACE_BUCKET_NAME/*"
          }
        ]
      }
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default
```

## `infra/iam/logs-irsa/role.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: logs-irsa-role
spec:
  forProvider:
    name: logs-irsa-role
    assumeRolePolicy: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Principal": {
              "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::REPLACE_ACCOUNT_ID:oidc-provider/REPLACE_OIDC_PROVIDER"
            },
            "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
            "Condition": {
              "StringEquals": {
                "REPLACE_OIDC_PROVIDER:sub": "system:serviceaccount:REPLACE_NAMESPACE:logs-writer",
                "REPLACE_OIDC_PROVIDER:aud": "sts.amazonaws.com"
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      }
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default
```

## `infra/iam/logs-irsa/role-policy-attachment.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: RolePolicyAttachment
metadata:
  name: logs-irsa-attachment
spec:
  forProvider:
    policyArnSelector:
      matchLabels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: logs-irsa-policy
    roleSelector:
      matchLabels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: logs-irsa-role
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default
```

Add labels so selectors work.

### Revised `policy.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: logs-irsa-policy
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: logs-irsa-policy
spec:
  forProvider:
    name: logs-irsa-policy
    description: Read/write access to logs bucket
    policy: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Sid": "ListBucket",
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": [
              "s3:ListBucket"
            ],
            "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::REPLACE_BUCKET_NAME"
          },
          {
            "Sid": "ObjectRW",
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": [
              "s3:GetObject",
              "s3:PutObject",
              "s3:DeleteObject"
            ],
            "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::REPLACE_BUCKET_NAME/*"
          }
        ]
      }
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default
```

### Revised `role.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: logs-irsa-role
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: logs-irsa-role
spec:
  forProvider:
    name: logs-irsa-role
    assumeRolePolicy: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Principal": {
              "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::REPLACE_ACCOUNT_ID:oidc-provider/REPLACE_OIDC_PROVIDER"
            },
            "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
            "Condition": {
              "StringEquals": {
                "REPLACE_OIDC_PROVIDER:sub": "system:serviceaccount:REPLACE_NAMESPACE:logs-writer",
                "REPLACE_OIDC_PROVIDER:aud": "sts.amazonaws.com"
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      }
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default
```

## `infra/iam/logs-irsa/serviceaccount.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: logs-writer
  namespace: default
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::REPLACE_ACCOUNT_ID:role/logs-irsa-role
```

---

# 3) Environment overlays

Use overlays to set:
- bucket name: `myapp-logs-dev` / `myapp-logs-prod`
- region if env-specific
- IAM trust details
- service account namespace if needed

---

## `overlays/dev/kustomization.yaml`
Add the new resources if your overlay aggregates infra directly:

```yaml
resources:
  - ../../infra/s3/logs
  - ../../infra/iam/logs-irsa
```

If your repo already has environment-specific infra aggregators, add them there instead.

```yaml
spec:

    region: us-east-1
```

```yaml
        "Version": "2012-10-17",

          {

            "Action": [
              "s3:ListBucket"
            ],
            "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev"
          },
          {

            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": [
              "s3:GetObject",

```

### `overlays/dev/logs-irsa-role-patch.yaml`

```yaml
    assumeRolePolicy: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Principal": {
              "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEV_OIDC_ID"
            },
            "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
            "Condition": {
              "StringEquals": {
                "oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEV_OIDC_ID:sub": "system:serviceaccount:default:logs-writer",
                "oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEV_OIDC_ID:aud": "sts.amazonaws.com"

            }

```

### `overlays/dev/logs-irsa-sa-patch.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: v1

metadata:
  name: logs-writer
  namespace: default

    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/logs-irsa-role-dev
```

Then reference those patches in `overlays/dev/kustomization.yaml`:

# 4) Flux Kustomization for separate reconciliation

Add a dedicated Flux object so the logs bucket reconciles independently.

## `flux/logs-bucket-kustomization.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: logs-bucket
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 10m
  prune: true
  sourceRef:
    kind: GitRepository
    name: knr-ops
  path: ./overlays/dev
  wait: true
```

Because Flux kustomizations are cluster-specific, this file usually differs per environment/cluster.

### For dev cluster
```yaml
spec:
  path: ./overlays/dev
```

### For prod cluster
```yaml
spec:
  path: ./overlays/prod
```

If your repo uses one `flux/kustomizations.yaml` file listing all Flux resources, add:

## `flux/kustomizations.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - logs-bucket-kustomization.yaml
```

Or append `- logs-bucket-kustomization.yaml` to the existing `resources:` list.

---

# 5) About SOPS

For this specific task, nothing here is inherently secret unless:
- you store account IDs/OIDC issuer values in encrypted env files, or
- your repo policy encrypts all environment config

If your repo uses SOPS for env patches, then put the IAM trust/account-specific values into encrypted replacement files instead of plaintext patches.

Typical example:
- `overlays/dev/logs-irsa-values.enc.yaml`
- `overlays/prod/logs-irsa-values.enc.yaml`

But strictly speaking, bucket names, account IDs, and OIDC issuer URLs are usually not secrets.

---

# 6) Notes / small fixes

## Least privilege
The policy above is read/write only to:
- the specific bucket
- objects under that bucket

No wildcard `s3:*`.

## Public access
Handled with:
- `blockPublicAcls: true`
- `blockPublicPolicy: true`
- `ignorePublicAcls: true`
- `restrictPublicBuckets: true`

## Versioning
Enabled via `BucketVersioning`.

## Encryption
AES256 via `BucketServerSideEncryptionConfiguration`.

---

# 7) Recommended final file tree

```text
infra/
  s3/
    logs/
      kustomization.yaml
      bucket.yaml
      versioning.yaml
      encryption.yaml
      public-access-block.yaml
  iam/
    logs-irsa/
      kustomization.yaml
      policy.yaml
      role.yaml
      role-policy-attachment.yaml
      serviceaccount.yaml

overlays/
  dev/
    kustomization.yaml
    logs-bucket-patch.yaml
    logs-versioning-patch.yaml
    logs-encryption-patch.yaml
    logs-pab-patch.yaml
    logs-irsa-policy-patch.yaml
    logs-irsa-role-patch.yaml
    logs-irsa-sa-patch.yaml
  prod/
    kustomization.yaml
    logs-bucket-patch.yaml
    logs-versioning-patch.yaml
    logs-encryption-patch.yaml
    logs-pab-patch.yaml
    logs-irsa-policy-patch.yaml
    logs-irsa-role-patch.yaml
    logs-irsa-sa-patch.yaml

flux/
  kustomizations.yaml
  logs-bucket-kustomization.yaml
```

---

# 8) One important caveat

Your prompt says:

- stack uses ACK
- but “Use ACK S3 CRDs (`s3.aws.upbound.io`)”

Those are not the same thing.

- **ACK S3** usually looks like: `s3.services.k8s.aws/...`
- **Upbound/Crossplane provider AWS** looks like: `s3.aws.upbound.io/...`

So before applying, align with whatever the repo already uses.

---

- `overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml`
- `flux/kustomizations.yaml`
- one existing S3 manifest from `infra/s3/`
- one existing IAM manifest from `infra/iam/`
